tagline.text: A natural fizzy-spring swimming pool in Catarman, Camiguin, fed by underground water at the foot of Mt. Hibok-Hibok

children.text: Bura Soda Water Swimming Pool is in Barangay Bura in Catarman, on the island of Camiguin. Two pools are filled with clear, cool soda water rising from an underground spring at the foot of Mt. Hibok-Hibok, giving you a swim that is typical of the volcanic island of Camiguin.

Bura Soda Water Pool is in Barangay Bura, Catarman, on the western side of Camiguin Island. Its address is on Compol-NIA-Mainit Road, and one blogger places it in the Sitio Lumad area. Camiguin is a volcanic island with hot and cold springs in many places, and this is described as a place that takes naturally rising soda water straight into its pools. One travel blog calls it the only soda pool in the Philippines, but that is the blogger's wording, so treat it as a reference only.

The pool lies at the foot of Mt. Hibok-Hibok. The resort is said to have been developed in 2007, which makes it relatively new compared with Camiguin's older attractions. Two mid-size pools are separated by a concrete trellis and surrounded by tropical trees and gardens. It is not large, so it suits a short stop to soak and rest during a Catarman sightseeing round rather than a long stay.

Reviews of the water and how it feels are fairly consistent. The water is clear and cool, and when you drink it, it tastes faintly sweet, with almost no fizz or sourness. One reviewer said it feels slightly tingly when you get in. Locals also say the water is good for the body, but this is not medically verified, so think of it as a cool swim rather than going for any health benefit.

Bura Soda Water Pool is not a large, showy sight like White Island or the Sunken Cemetery. In return, admission is low and the facilities are simple, so it is easy to drop in for a short while on a half day around the Camiguin circumferential road. Admission, opening days and hours differ slightly between sources, so please check before you go. The prices and hours in this guide are based on posts from 2024–2025 and the local government's tourism information.

blocks.title: Two pools filled with soda water

children.text: The two pools that take water straight from the underground spring are the main attraction. They are separated by a concrete trellis, and there are shallow and deep areas, so children and adults can play together. The pool water is not for drinking, so be careful not to swallow it.

Apart from the pools, there is an area with taps where you can collect drinkable water. Many reviews say it tastes faintly sweet and has no bubbles. If you bring an empty bottle, you can take some cool spring water home. There is also a mention that bottled soda water is sold as a souvenir at the facility.

blocks.title: A forest setting on the Mt. Hibok-Hibok slope

children.text: The surroundings are landscaped with dense trees and gardens, so it is pleasant to sit and rest even if you do not get in the water. You can feel the atmosphere typical of Camiguin, with the volcano's slopes continuing behind the pools. It is a good place for scenery photos, but the ground near the water is wet and slippery, so be careful when walking in shoes.

The facility has cottages and picnic tables where you can leave your things and rest. Catarman's tourism information lists a cottage at about ₱150 for 3 hours. If you plan to bring lunch or snacks, renting a cottage is more convenient, but the fee and time unit may change, so check on site.

There are men's and women's toilets, changing rooms and showers, so you can change clothes after swimming. It is a good place to rinse off during a Camiguin island tour. Bring your own towel, a change of clothes and a waterproof bag.

The restaurant inside the facility was reportedly closed at the time of one review. Instead, there are several sari-sari stores just outside the entrance where you can buy drinks and snacks, and there is also mention that you can order food from a nearby restaurant. It is safer to decide on your meal in advance.

blocks.title: A middle stop on a Catarman sightseeing route

children.text: Tuasan Falls, Sto. Niño Cold Spring, the Sunken Cemetery and the Guiob Church ruins are all in the same Catarman area, so they combine well into one day. One reviewer says it is about 8 km and 15 minutes by multicab (a small shared vehicle) from the Sunken Cemetery viewing point. Putting a cool swim in the hot afternoon makes the schedule much easier.

items.title: Catarman half-day route
items.subtitle: Sunken Cemetery and the soda water pool

children.text: Have breakfast in Mambajao town, then hire a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) or tricycle, or rent a motorbike.
Head toward Catarman and see the Guiob Church ruins and the Sunken Cemetery viewpoint.
Have lunch near the Sunken Cemetery, then go to Bura Soda Water Pool. It is described as about
15 minutes
by multicab.
Swim in the pool and try the soda water. Renting a cottage to rest is also a good idea.
Shower and change, then visit one more nearby sight, such as Tuasan Falls or Sto. Niño Cold Spring.
If your schedule is tight, you can skip the waterfall. The pool is said to be open until 5 p.m., so arrive before then.

items.title: Camiguin full-day tour
items.subtitle: Falls, hot spring and soda water pool

children.text: First see the northern sights, such as Katibawasan Falls and Ardent Hot Spring in Mambajao.
Move on to Catarman and see Tongatok Cove viewpoint and the old church ruins.
Have an early lunch.
After Tuasan Falls, rest at Bura Soda Water Pool in the middle of the afternoon.
Finish at the Sunken Cemetery.
This order is based on an itinerary from one travel blog, and the times are estimates. They change with travel speed and road conditions, so leave some margin.

items.title: Flight from Manila to Cagayan de Oro

children.text: There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Laguindingan Airport (CGY) in Cagayan de Oro. Airlines and times change by season, so check on a booking site.

From Laguindingan Airport you head toward Cagayan de Oro city and then take a bus bound for Balingoan. Check the airport transfer options and the bus terminal location at the information desk or the airport taxi booth after you arrive.
Whether there are flights to and from Camiguin varies by season, so check first.

items.title: Bus and ferry from Cagayan de Oro to Camiguin

children.text: Take a bus from Cagayan de Oro to Balingoan port, then a ferry from Balingoan to Benoni port in Camiguin.
After landing at Benoni port, find a multicab or motorbike to Barangay Bura in Catarman.
Bus and ferry times and fares change, so check the operators' notices before you leave.
From Mambajao town it is about
35 minutes
by motorbike along the Camiguin circumferential road according to one review, and another review says it is shorter by car.
Hiring a tricycle or habal-habal is described as about
one way, but it depends on negotiation and the season.
If you rent a motorbike, one review says you can park it outside the entrance for free.
Search Google Maps for "Soda Water Pool" or "Bura Soda Water Pool" to find the spot on Compol-NIA-Mainit Road.
Map apps can be weak in some places, so download an offline map beforehand.

Bura Soda Water Pool can be visited year-round with no special season. Camiguin is a rainy island, so the drier months are said to be relatively better. One local government tourism guide lists it among the places people visit often in spring.

On weekends, local holidays and school breaks, local families come and it gets crowded. One reviewer wrote that it was busy during the children's summer break. For a quieter visit, weekday mornings are better.

Roads are slippery after showers, so take care and leave room in your schedule

There are not many large lodgings near the pool, and most travelers stay in Mambajao or Catarman town. Since this is a stop on a Camiguin island tour, you can choose where to stay based on your whole itinerary.

The restaurant inside the facility was recorded as closed at the time of one review. You can buy snacks and drinks at the sari-sari stores outside the entrance and order food from a nearby restaurant. For a meal after swimming, it is better to use restaurants in Catarman town or near the Sunken Cemetery. Business status can change, so check on site. Seafood and local dishes are available all over Camiguin, so the easiest option is to have lunch at a restaurant you like along your tour route.
Admission differs by source, so bring plenty of cash and small bills in case there is no change.
Bring swimwear, a towel, a change of clothes and a waterproof bag, and keep valuables on you rather than leaving them in the cottage.
Collect drinking water from the taps, not from the pool. Bring an empty bottle.
One local government guide lists opening days as Tuesday to Sunday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and one review says it is closed on Mondays. Check in advance if you plan to go on a Monday.
Weekday mornings are quiet, while weekends and school breaks are crowded.
The edges of the pool are wet and slippery, so keep hold of your child's hand.
Combining Tuasan Falls, Sto. Niño Cold Spring and the Sunken Cemetery saves travel time.
Phone signal and map apps can be weak, so download an offline map.
The pool water is not drinking water. Collect drinking water only from the designated taps.
Admission and opening days differ by source and may differ on site, so check the latest information.
Claims about health benefits are not verified, so if you have a medical condition, consult a doctor before using it.
The restaurant inside may be closed, so prepare snacks and water in advance.
After rain the road and the area around the pool are slippery.
If you ride a motorbike yourself, wear a helmet and watch the curves and wet roads on the circumferential road.

blocks.title: Sunken Cemetery & Guiob Church Ruins, Camiguin

children.text: It is described as about
15 minutes
and
8 km
away by multicab. You can see the cross of the cemetery that sank in a volcanic eruption out on the sea.
It is in the same Catarman area, so it can be combined with the soda water pool into one route. Check on site whether it is open.
Another spring attraction in Catarman, and many reviews mention visiting it on the same day.
For the whole-island itinerary and other sights, see the Camiguin entry.
